We couldn\'t confirm it\'s you, so nothing was changed.
The last picture from {tv}. Tap to refresh.
Switches off the usual clutter and keeps everything else.
Lets you choose each item yourself.
The TV keeps its own. See why
The TV\'s own is in use
The Home button opens it. The TV\'s own stays on.
The TV turned its own home screen back on.
Shown as apps: this TV keeps its own home screen
{count, plural, one {# app is better switched back on} other {# apps are better switched back on}}

{count, plural, one {Held through # restart} other {Held through # restarts}}
It counts for this TV model. You see what goes first.
You told us on {date}. Thank you.
The TV\'s own home screen came back after a restart.
Tell us, so we can look at this TV model.
To change things on the TV, debugging needs to be on for a moment.
On the TV: Settings > Device Preferences > Developer options > USB debugging. We\'ll take it from there and switch it off again when we\'re done.
You won\'t need to press Build again. Developer options stays unlocked.
It\'s off because we switched it off when we were done last time, as planned.
Join the same Wi-Fi as the TV. We\'ll carry on by ourselves.
Look at the TV and allow this phone
The TV is asking \"Allow USB debugging?\". Tick \"Always allow\", then choose Allow (OK on some TVs).
The code on the TV ends in {tail}. That is this phone.
Waiting for your tap on the TV...
Join the same Wi-Fi as the TV.
Same network as when this TV was set up
Your network changed since setup. We\'re looking for the TV on this one.
The TV answers at its saved address
Switch on USB debugging on the TV. If it\'s on, the TV may have a new address.
The TV was found at another address on this network
Nothing on this Wi-Fi answered as this TV yet. We keep looking.
The TV is waiting for you to allow this phone
Look at the TV: tick Always allow, then choose Allow.

Still nothing? Some TVs open the Wi-Fi debugging port only after a restart, so restart the TV once. Some also need \"Network debugging\" or \"Wireless debugging\" switched on as well as USB debugging. And the TV may have a new address: it shows on the TV under Settings > Network.
The TV answers at the address you typed
Check the address on the TV under Settings > Network. USB debugging must be on there too.
Looking at the Wi-Fi and your TVs...
Copied. Paste it into a message or an issue.
We look at the Wi-Fi and each saved TV for about 10 seconds, then copy what we saw. It has the names you gave your TVs, but never a Wi-Fi name, a whole address, a serial number or a key.
What the app sees of your Wi-Fi and TVs, to copy or share
The TV stopped answering partway through. Carry on with the rest, or undo what we did. Until then nothing else can change on this TV.
We stopped partway through. Carry on with the rest, or undo what we did. Until then nothing else can change on this TV.
The setup of {tv} didn\'t finish. Open it to carry on or undo what we did.
The TV didn\'t answer. Check that it\'s on and on the same Wi-Fi as this phone, then try again.
{tv} changed since we last read it
Something on the TV changed after we read it, so we stopped before changing anything. Nothing was changed. Check the TV again and we\'ll start from what it has now.
Something on the TV changed after we read it, so we stopped partway through. Check the TV again to carry on from what it has now, or undo what we did.
Once {app} was back on, the TV gave it the Home button, so Home no longer opens the new home screen. Switch {app} off again to get the new one back, or keep it.
Nothing else changed. Send it again, or undo to keep the look the TV had. Until then nothing else can change on this TV.
Each one can be put back. Nothing is deleted; \"off\" means asleep.
Needed for the new home screen
The list for this TV now keeps it on.
Nothing is switched off right now.
Everything on the TV is switched on.
{count, plural, one {# thing came back after an update. Switch it off again?} other {# things came back after an update. Switch them off again?}}
Nothing came back. All as you left it.
We couldn\'t check just now. Is the TV still on?
{count, plural, one {# thing came back on the TV.} other {# things came back on the TV.}}
Back to Simple hides the extra options. Your TV stays as it is.
This deletes the record of this TV, its journals and its restore points from this phone. The TV itself is not changed, but you won\'t be able to undo from this phone afterwards.
Setup is still working on this TV. Wait for it to finish or stop it first.
Text size follows the size set in your phone\'s Settings.
Small taps when something finishes or needs you.
Kept in a dedicated security chip (StrongBox).
Kept in the phone\'s secure hardware (TEE).
Kept in software, wrapped with a key from the phone\'s secure storage. This phone can\'t hold it in hardware.

Nothing leaves your network except downloads from github.com. GitHub sees your phone\'s address and a generic user agent. A report leaves the phone only when you copy, share or post it yourself.
Nothing leaves your network. The app talks only to the TV you pick and makes no internet requests of its own. A report leaves the phone only when you copy, share or post it yourself.
See the report first, then share it or post it on GitHub
Every TV will ask to trust this phone again.
Reset the key on this phone?
Deletes every TV record, journal, restore point, the app\'s diagnostics log and the key from this phone. The TVs themselves are not changed, and you won\'t be able to undo from this phone afterwards.
Setup is still working on {tv}. Wait for it to finish or stop it first.
We stop here and put back what we changed so far. Your TV stays safe.
We keep what is already done and change nothing else. Your TV stays safe.
Undo the changes on the TV?
We put back everything this change did, so the TV is as it was before. Nothing is deleted.
We haven\'t met this exact TV before, so we were careful with it. A short report from you helps us add it.
You sent this TV\'s report on {date}. We\'ll post in your issue when there\'s news.
The setup wizard can take the Home button
Switch the TV\'s own home screen back on so the TV keeps starting normally.
Switching the TV\'s own home screen back on...
This report says what this TV is and which apps it came with, so we can make a list for it. Apps you installed yourself are only counted, never named.
This says the new home screen held on this TV, with the TV\'s model and what the app counted. Nothing else: no names, no addresses.
No restart has been counted on this TV yet. Restart it once with the app connected, then try again.
This report has the steps we ran and a short summary of the TV, as plain text. Addresses, serial numbers, keys and codes are removed first. The steps can name apps we switched off or tried to.
This is public if you post it on GitHub. The app sends nothing itself: you choose where it goes.
We copy the report, then open the form on GitHub. Paste it into the box that asks for it.
The form on GitHub opens with this report already in it. Add a few words if you like, then post it. We copy the report too, in case the form opens without it.

The form on GitHub opens with this report in it, with only the newest lines of the log so that it fits. Add a few words if you like, then post it. We copy the whole report too, in case we ask for the rest.
This report is too long to go into the form by itself, so we copy it for you. On GitHub, long-press the report box, choose Paste, then post it.
We need to read this TV once before we can make its report. Set it up or connect to it, then try again.
You sent this TV\'s report on {date}. We\'ll post in your issue when there\'s news. You can send it again.
Your issue: {issue}. Open it to see the news.
Paste the link of the issue the report went to, and we\'ll remember it here.
That isn\'t a link to an issue of this app on GitHub.
